record.paper_title: Nuclei of Seyfert galaxies and QSOs - Central engine & conditions of star formation: Workshop summary and open questions
record.context_brief: high-redshift AGN triggering and host evolution
record.original_question: At high redshift, how is active-galactic-nucleus activity triggered, what are the characteristics of active-galactic-nucleus host galaxies, and how does the relation between black-hole accretion and host-galaxy star formation evolve with redshift?

evidence.quote: Some of the key questions in the high redshift session were how AGN activity is triggered, what are the characteristics of AGN hosts at high-z, and how does the relation between the AGN and the star formation in the host galaxy evolve with redshift.
The reliability of black hole mass estimates and new method to explore the inner region of AGN using gravitational lensing were also discussed.

artifact.category_tag: high-redshift AGN triggering and host galaxies
artifact.self_contained_problem:
An active galactic nucleus (AGN) is the compact, highly luminous central region of a galaxy whose energy output is powered by accretion of matter onto a supermassive black hole (SMBH) at its center. The host galaxy of an AGN is the galaxy in which the SMBH resides. Star formation rate (SFR) denotes the mass of new stars formed per unit time in the host, while the black-hole accretion rate (BHAR) is the mass per unit time accreted onto the SMBH (typically inferred from the AGN bolometric luminosity divided by a radiative efficiency). The redshift z parameterizes cosmic epoch, with high redshift conventionally meaning z ≳ 1.

Address the following three interrelated questions concerning AGN at high redshift:

(a) Triggering mechanisms. By what physical processes is AGN activity initiated and fueled at high redshift? In particular, determine the relative importance, as a function of redshift z and AGN luminosity, of (i) major galaxy mergers, (ii) minor mergers and tidal interactions, (iii) secular processes such as bar- or disk-instability-driven gas inflow, and (iv) cosmological cold-gas accretion from the intergalactic medium, in delivering gas to within the SMBH sphere of influence and powering accretion.

(b) Host-galaxy characteristics. Characterize the statistical properties of high-redshift AGN host galaxies, including their stellar masses, morphologies (disk vs. spheroid vs. disturbed/merger fractions), colors and positions relative to the star-forming main sequence, gas fractions, dust content, and environments, and quantify how these properties differ from those of mass-matched non-AGN galaxies at the same redshift.

(c) Coevolution of accretion and star formation. Determine the functional form and redshift evolution of the relation between BHAR and host SFR, including: the mean ⟨BHAR⟩ as a function of SFR (and conversely ⟨SFR⟩ as a function of AGN luminosity), the scatter of this relation, and how the ratio BHAR/SFR evolves with z. Establish whether this relation is consistent with a constant scaling, with the cosmic-time evolution of the SMBH-to-stellar-mass ratio M_BH/M_*, and with feedback-regulated coevolution scenarios.

Provide observational and/or theoretical determinations supporting the answers.
artifact.status_search_result: The questions of how AGN are triggered at high redshift, the characterization of their host galaxies, and the redshift evolution of the AGN–star formation connection remain active areas of research. No consensus answers exist; numerous recent studies (e.g., from JWST, ALMA, and X-ray surveys) continue to debate merger vs. secular triggering, host main-sequence offsets, and the form of BHAR–SFR scaling, indicating the problem is open.

status_evidence.title: The AGN-Star Formation Connection: Future Prospects with JWST
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews the still-debated relation between black hole accretion and host star formation across cosmic time.
status_evidence.claim: The AGN–SFR coevolution relation across redshift remains under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Triggering mechanisms of AGN at high redshift
status_evidence.snippet: Recent studies continue to assess the relative roles of mergers and secular processes in fueling high-z AGN.
status_evidence.claim: AGN triggering at high redshift is not settled; mergers vs. secular processes still debated.
